subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should an ignore file larger than 4 MiB intentionally make its entire scanned subtree invisible, rather than preserving the existing fail-open discovery behavior?
rationale: The cap and whole-subtree exclusion trade compatibility for memory safety and conservative discovery; repository policy treats a new fail-closed behavior as an explicit security and upgrade decision rather than an implementation detail.

options.title: Approve terminal fail-closed behavior
options.body: Keep the 4 MiB cap, ensure the subtree deny is applied last or terminates processing, and require compatibility documentation and current-head proof.

options.title: Preserve fail-open compatibility
options.body: Bound and skip the oversized file while continuing discovery, accepting that exclusions from the unread policy cannot be enforced.

options.title: Redesign oversized-file handling
options.body: Pause this PR and choose a streaming parser or another policy that avoids both unbounded buffering and unconditional subtree removal.

recommendation.title: Approve terminal fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Keep the 4 MiB cap, ensure the subtree deny is applied last or terminates processing, and require compatibility documentation and current-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to the central skill-loading path that consumes the ignore matcher, though an explicit repository owner should make the final policy choice.
